detail.abstract: This study investigates how Bloom Greens, a health supplement brand, leveraged TikTok's short-form video platform to achieve rapid growth through influencer marketing. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research combines quantitative data from influencer surveys with qualitative thematic analysis to explore the effectiveness of Bloom's TikTok strategies. The survey, distributed to over 200 influencers and receiving 30 responses, revealed that micro-influencers (10k-200k followers) generated higher engagement and authenticity compared to macro-influencers. Influencers who genuinely supported the product created more effective content, emphasizing the importance of authenticity and creative freedom in brand partnerships. The research finds that Bloom Greens' success is rooted in its alignment with TikTok's algorithm-driven, highly personalized content model, and its strategic partnerships with relatable influencers. While effective, the brand's heavy reliance on micro-influencers may limit future scalability. This paper contributes to the understanding of digital marketing trends and provides insight into how social media platforms like TikTok can be used to cultivate consumer trust and brand loyalty.

detail.abstract: Digital marketing has rapidly transformed the Indian pharmaceutical industry, especially in how companies engage with healthcare professionals (HCPs) for prescription product promotion. This scoping review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature, case studies, and select grey sources from 2014 to 2024, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework was applied to interpret HCP adoption behavior. The findings reveal a strong shift toward digital-first strategies, particularly after COVID-19, with rising adoption of e-detailing, WhatsApp-based outreach, AI-powered CRM systems, and omnichannel campaigns. Notably, over 70% of studies published post-2020 emphasized mobile-based and AI-enabled personalization tools for targeted engagement. While personalization and platform integration have improved outreach, there remains limited evidence of long-term return on investment (ROI) and real-world clinical outcomes. Persistent challenges include uneven digital literacy among field forces, regulatory ambiguity, and gaps in measuring marketing effectiveness. Strengthening compliance, fostering HCP trust, and embedding outcome-driven digital strategies will be critical to building a robust and ethical digital marketing ecosystem in India's pharmaceutical sector.

title: Interactive Context Refinement (ICR): Contextual Blindness in Generative AI Systems
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Interactive Context Refinement (ICR): Contextual Blindness in Generative AI Systems
detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across domains such as education, healthcare, and customer support. However, their inability to fully grasp user context-termed contextual blindness-leads to hallucinations, inaccurate personalization, and diminished user trust. This paper introduces Interactive Context Refinement (ICR), a dialoguedriven framework that enables generative AI systems to proactively refine user context before generating responses. We present the architecture, implementation, and evaluation of an ICR prototype, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing hallucinations and improving response accuracy across multiple domains.

title: Pricing in Live Streaming E-Commerce: Integrating Customer Type Analysis
affiliations: Temple University - Fox School of Business and Management, Northeastern University (USA) - D’Amore-McKim School of Business and Temple University - Department of Statistics, Operations, and Data Science

detail.title: Pricing in Live Streaming E-Commerce: Integrating Customer Type Analysis
detail.abstract: Live streaming e-commerce (LSE) is gradually becoming the future of shopping and creates hundreds of billions of market. Influencers can demonstrate the product and interact with potential consumers in real-time on LSE platforms, reducing product uncertainty and raising the consumers' purchasing intention. In this research, we focus on understanding how online stores alter LSE frequency and pricing decisions to boost their revenue. To better understand consumers' decisions, we also categorize consumers into product-oriented and influencer-oriented, aiming to understand the impact of consumer heterogeneity on store decisions. Our research makes both theoretical and practical contributions. On the one hand, we enrich the prior literature by focusing on exploring more nuanced decisions that a store can make regarding the LSE setting and adoption while considering customers' heterogeneity. On the other hand, our research findings can help online stores make better decisions and strategies for leveraging LSE to boost their product sales and revenue.

detail.abstract: This empirical study investigates the factors influencing green purchase intentions and green consumption behavior among Generation Z using SmartPLS for analysis and data collected from over 298 respondents. The study focuses on the role of social media engagement, environmental awareness, green advertising perception, social media influencers advocacy, and platform features in shaping sustainable consumption patterns. Results reveal that social media engagement and environmental awareness significantly impact green purchase intentions, demonstrating the importance of digital interaction and environmental knowledge among Generation Z. Furthermore, the study highlights the positive influence of credible green advertising, social media influencers advocacy, and engaging platform features in enhancing green purchase intentions. The findings confirm that green purchase intentions significantly drive green consumption behavior, emphasizing the importance of aligning marketing strategies and digital tools with the values of this demographic. By providing a detailed examination of these relationships, the study offers actionable insights for stakeholders, including businesses, policymakers, and educators, to design strategies that effectively promote sustainable behaviors. This research contributes to the growing literature on sustainability and digital engagement, offering a robust framework for understanding the drivers of environmentally conscious consumption in the digital age.

title: Dark Data Consulting: Turning Unused Data into Strategic Advantage for Businesses
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Dark Data Consulting: Turning Unused Data into Strategic Advantage for Businesses
detail.abstract: Dark data—information collected by organizations but left unutilized—represents a significant untapped resource for strategic decision-making. This thesis investigates the barriers to leveraging dark data, including technical, organizational, and ethical challenges, and evaluates its potential to drive competitive advantage. Using a mixed-method approach combining conceptual analysis with empirical case studies, we propose a novel consulting framework to transform dark data into actionable insights. The study integrates theoretical perspectives, such as the Resource-Based View and Socio-Technical Theory, to address gaps in current data consulting practices. Findings highlight the critical role of structured governance, crossfunctional collaboration, and advanced analytics in unlocking dark data's value. This research contributes to the academic discourse on data management and offers practical recommendations for organizations aiming to integrate dark data into strategic decisionmaking processes.

title: Algorithmic Remedies for Google's Data Monopoly
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: Algorithmic Remedies for Google's Data Monopoly
detail.abstract:
Algorithms and data are the building blocks of the digital economy. From Google’s search engine to Meta’s Instagram and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, all “Big Tech” rely on algorithms to collect and process vast amounts of data that power their services and AI models. While algorithms themselves can be efficient and impartial tools, Google’s strategic use of them, combined with exclusionary practices, has landed the company in federal court for monopolizing critical digital markets. Later this year, judges are expected to determine the remedies to address this conduct; a decision that will de facto regulate data-driven markets and influence the future of the emerging AI industry.

Under one such remedy, courts could require Google to grant rivals access to key data facilities. However, such data-sharing obligations in antitrust law create a classic resource allocation problem: who gets access, and how can courts ensure that access is fair and non-discriminatory? This article demonstrates that this legal challenge mirrors a problem computer science solved decades ago: ensuring multiple parties can use a shared resource without conflict. Thereafter, drawing on those algorithmic solutions, it proposes a framework with systems that operate like a digital ‘take-a-number’ machine or a formal voting process to manage data distribution efficiently and fairly. 

This article makes three important contributions to the existing scholarship in this field. First, it explains how data-sharing remedies can be designed and implemented, whether to address specific anticompetitive conduct or as part of broader regulatory frameworks. Second, it develops a comprehensive framework with three algorithmic approaches for resource allocation, translating computer science solutions into legal mechanisms. Third, this framework is applied to Google’s ongoing monopolization cases, demonstrating how these mechanisms can foster competition in AI and other data-driven markets.

detail.abstract: Despite its significance, there is limited knowledge about the development of auditor expertise throughout a professional career. To address this gap, this study examined how diverse career experiences contribute to the formation of auditing expertise. Drawing on career theories, it introduced the concept of an "experience portfolio"-the cumulative set of heterogeneous job experiences acquired through career transitions. Using a novel survey of 485 audit partners from the Japanese Big 4 firms, this analysis isolates experience-based effects by leveraging Japan's highly selective and demographically homogeneous audit labor market. The results show that while frequent transitions are associated with delayed promotion, certain types of experiences contribute distinct benefits. For example, a global audit experience is associated with more complex client assignments, whereas non-audit roles such as IPO advisory services and regulatory inspections support the management of larger client portfolios. These findings reconceptualize auditor expertise as the outcome of varied nonlinear career paths, challenging traditional metrics such as tenure or specialization. This study introduces a typology of experience, offering theoretical insights into expertise development and practical implications for human capital management and regulatory policies.

title: The Costs of Opening an Umbrella: How Store-Brand Umbrella Rebranding Affects National Brand Profits
affiliations: University of Amsterdam - Amsterdam Business School and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Marketing Area

detail.title: The Costs of Opening an Umbrella: How Store-Brand Umbrella Rebranding Affects National Brand Profits
detail.abstract: Retailers can unify their store brands (SB) and rebrand them under a common brand name, a strategy known as umbrella branding, to strengthen the united SB. But this tactic also might trigger unanticipated consequences for the profits that retailers make on the national brands (NB) they offer. Due to the confidential nature of profits and a typical focus on SBs' own outcomes, these changes remain understudied, even though NBs have a substantial influence on retailers' overall performance. To bridge this gap, the current research relies on proprietary, detailed, closely guarded profit data, including NB wholesale prices, retail prices, and sales, for 250 brands and more than 1,300 products, gathered in the context of a retailer's umbrella rebranding initiative for its SBs. Using the synthetic difference-indifferences method, the study shows that NB profits decrease substantially, though it also reveals considerable heterogeneity, spanning both increases and decreases. Leveraging this heterogeneity, the paper assesses the role of three supply chain-related mechanisms to understand why NB profits change. By identifying the thus far neglected effects of an SB umbrella rebranding on suppliers of NBs, this study reveals additional costs to retailers, along with some practical insights for mitigating them and avoiding additional channel conflicts.

title: Navigating the Ethical and Legal Frontiers of Hyperpersonalization in the Digital Age
affiliations: Institute of Management & Technology

detail.title: Navigating the Ethical and Legal Frontiers of Hyperpersonalization in the Digital Age
detail.abstract: Hyper personalization has emerged as a powerful marketing strategy, enabling firms to deliver highly tailored content, products, and services by leveraging real-time data, artificial intelligence, and behavioural analytics. While this precision marketing enhances consumer engagement and improves ROI, it simultaneously raises complex legal and ethical concerns. The line between relevance and manipulation is increasingly blurred, as hyper personalization often occurs without fully informed consent or meaningful transparency 1. Issues of data privacy, algorithmic discrimination, digital autonomy, and dark patterns demand closer scrutiny. This paper critically examines the ethical and legal implications of hyper-personalization in consumerfacing industries, particularly in marketing and digital advertising. It will analysis the ethical background of hyper-personalization through theories of Rawl's theory of justice, Kantian ethics, Utilitarianism, Social Contract Theory. It will also looks into right based ethics extensively to analyse the legal environment where the current market is emerging around. Adopting an interdisciplinary methodology, it draws from marketing theory, digital ethics, and global legal frameworks most notably the GDPR, CCPA, and proposed AI regulations. Through illustrative case studies (e.g., Cambridge Analytica, Amazon's dynamic pricing), the paper explores how personalization can both empower and exploit consumers. Key findings emphasize the need for clearer standards on consumer consent, consumer awareness, algorithmic transparency, and ethical data use. The paper proposes a hybrid framework combining ethical marketing principles with regulatory compliance to guide future practices. It concludes with actionable recommendations for marketers, legal practitioners, and policymakers to ensure that hyperpersonalization supports consumer trust, regulatory integrity, and sustainable brand.

title: The New Playbook for Air Cargo Distribution- From Phone Calls to Platforms: How E-Booking is Reshaping Air Cargo

detail.abstract:
This paper studies how air cargo booking is moving from phone calls and emails to online platforms. We compare the old, people-driven model with the new digital model using industry sources from 2015–2025 and examples from WebCargo by Freightos, cargo.one, CargoAi, Octoloop (India), and airline portals. We also explain how General Sales and Service Agents (GSSAs) work today, which is on commission, mark-up/allotment, and minimum guarantee, and how their role is changing.

Our findings are simple. Air cargo sales are still largely manual, but e-booking has grown fast in the last few years. Airlines are building an “omnichannel” mix: direct portals/APIs, marketplaces, and traditional sales teams/GSSAs. Forwarders value instant rates, 24×7 access, and faster confirmation, but they still want human support for complex cargo and exceptions. GSSAs are not disappearing but they are adapting and adding or planning to add digital tools, data, and customer service around online bookings. Dynamic pricing and real-time capacity are expanding but not yet universal. Adoption varies by region: Europe leads, North America is catching up, and parts of Asia (including India) are moving steadily, helped by local platforms like Octoloop that open access for smaller forwarders.

The paper offers a practical roadmap for each stakeholder. Airlines should modernise systems, manage channels together, and strengthen revenue management. GSSAs should invest in technology and focus on service beyond the basic booking. Forwarders should integrate digital tools into daily work and use data to serve shippers faster. Overall, the near future is a hybrid model where routine shipments will be booked online, while people will handle special cargo, service recovery, and relationships.

title: Notes on a World with Generative AI
affiliations: IZA Institute of Labor Economics

detail.title: Notes on a World with Generative AI

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are moving into domains once seen as uniquely human: reasoning, synthesis, abstraction, and rhetoric. Addressed to labor economists and informed readers, this paper clarifies what is truly new about LLMs, what is not, and why it matters. Using an analogy to auto-regressive models from economics, we explain their stochastic nature, whose fluency is often mistaken for agency. We place LLMs in the longer history of human: machine outsourcing, from digestion to cognition, and examine disruptive effects on white-collar labor, institutions, and epistemic norms. Risks emerge when synthetic content becomes both product and input, creating feedback loops that erode originality and reliability. Grounding the discussion in conceptual clarity over hype, we argue that while GenAI may substitute for some labor, statistical limits will, probably but not without major disruption, preserve a key role for human judgment. The question is not only how these tools are used, but which tasks we relinquish and how we reallocate expertise in a new division of cognitive labor.

detail.abstract: This qualitative study investigated the role of social media marketing in increasing brand awareness among small businesses in NBBS Proper, Navotas City. With social media platforms allowing greater accessibility (Facebook is available on most mobile devices, and TikTok is easily stored), small and microentrepreneurs are engaging with customers to market their products, as well as give their brands a wider reach. This study conducted a focus group discussion to better understand how social media marketing impacts brand awareness, with five participants intentionally chosen due to their ownership of small businesses with an online presence. Thematic analysis revealed four primary themes: the predominance of Facebook as a marketing channel, the role of social media in enhancing visibility, the limitations of time and digital skills, and the success of community-driven initiatives, such as giveaways or local hashtags. The results suggest that although participants felt limited by their time, lack of digital proficiency, and scarce efforts to sell their product, they also displayed an ability to adapt using free and organic marketing methods. The overall contribution of this study is its unyielding illustration of how social media marketing is crucial and empowering for grassroots brands to build brand awareness within a digital-first and competitive marketplace.

title: Causal Returns to Education
affiliations: University of Arkansas, Fayetteville and Georgetown University

detail.title: Causal Returns to Education

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Using 182 estimates from 140 studies in 55 countries, this paper compares ordinary least
squares (OLS) and instrumental variables (IV) estimates of the private returns to schooling.
IV returns average 9.7 percent—38 percent higher than OLS—and exceed OLS in nearly
80 percent of cases, with the largest gaps in developing countries. These patterns align
with theories of diminishing marginal returns, scarcity rents, and attenuation from
measurement error. While IV methods mitigate bias, instrument validity and external validity
concerns persist. Evidence consistently shows substantial causal returns, particularly for
disadvantaged populations, underscoring the need for rigorous research.

title: Stock Market Performance and GDP Growth in Nepal
affiliations: Nepal Open University(NOU)

detail.title: Stock Market Performance and GDP Growth in Nepal
detail.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between stock market performance and economic growth in Nepal, employing the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds testing approach and Granger causality analysis using annual time-series data from 1994 to 2024. The results confirm a long-run association between stock market indicators and GDP growth, with market capitalisation and the number of listed companies exerting significant positive effects on economic growth. Interest rates positively influence stock market performance, while inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index, negatively affects both GDP and market growth in the short run. Granger causality tests reveal bidirectional relationships between GDP and market capitalisation, as well as between market capitalisation and interest rates, inflation, and the number of listed companies. The error correction term confirms a long-run equilibrium, indicating that stock market fluctuations have a sustained impact on economic stability. The findings underscore the importance of macroeconomic stability, regulatory reforms, and investor confidence in enhancing the stock market's role as a driver of economic growth. Policy recommendations include strengthening market transparency, improving regulatory frameworks, managing interest rates effectively, and implementing targeted inflation control measures. The study offers valuable insights for policymakers, investors, and researchers seeking to deepen the link between stock market performance and sustainable economic growth in Nepal.

title: Synthesizing Evidence: Data-Pooling as a Tool for Treatment Selection in Online Experiments
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management and The Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Synthesizing Evidence: Data-Pooling as a Tool for Treatment Selection in Online Experiments
detail.abstract: Randomized experiments are the gold standard for causal inference but face significant challenges in business applications, including limited traffic allocation, the need for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation, and the complexity of managing overlapping experiments. These factors lead to high variability in treatment effect estimates, making data-driven policy roll-out difficult. To address these issues, we introduce the data-pooling treatment roll-out (DPTR) framework, which enhances policy roll-out by pooling data across experiments rather than focusing narrowly on individual ones. DPTR can effectively accommodate both overlapping and non-overlapping traffic scenarios, regardless of linear or nonlinear model specifications. We demonstrate the framework's robustness through a three-pronged validation: (a) theoretical analysis shows that DPTR surpasses the traditional difference-in-mean and ordinary least squares methods under nonoverlapping experiments, particularly when the number of experiments is large; (b) synthetic simulations confirm its adaptability in complex scenarios with overlapping traffic, rich covariates and nonlinear specifications; and (c) empirical applications to two experimental datasets from real-world platforms, demonstrating its effectiveness in guiding customized policy roll-outs for subgroups within a single experiment, as well as in coordinating policy deployments across multiple experiments with overlapping scenarios. By reducing estimation variability to improve decision-making effectiveness, DPTR provides a scalable, practical solution for online platforms to better leverage their experimental data in today's increasingly complex business environments.

title: The Structural Immunity Problem: Why Parallel Systems Become Necessary
affiliations: Epistria

detail.title: The Structural Immunity Problem: Why Parallel Systems Become Necessary
detail.abstract: When AI-driven decision systems develop climate lock, organizations instinctively reach for familiar solutions: better training data, improved algorithms, cultural change initiatives, enhanced oversight. This response treats climate lock as an operational defect requiring technical remedy. But climate lock is not a malfunction-it is a survival adaptation gone pathological. Both human and AI systems adopt comfort-seeking patterns for the same fundamental reason: to reduce uncertainty and preserve stability. This paper demonstrates why fighting comfort requires acknowledging a deeper truth about adaptive systems: the very mechanisms that ensure short-term survival eventually constrain long-term adaptability. Traditional interventions fail not because they are poorly designed, but because they operate within the same philosophical framework that created the problem. Parallel systems become necessary not as an optimization choice, but as a structural requirement for preserving metaawareness in locked systems.

title: Output Fluctuations and Firm Recruitment Effort
affiliations: University of Edinburgh, University of Lille III, University of London and University of London - Royal Holloway College

detail.title: Output Fluctuations and Firm Recruitment Effort

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between output fluctuations and firms' recruitment efforts using Danish data that link online job ads with high-frequency firm-level revenue and value-added. While overall output growth is weakly correlated with advertisement rates, decomposing output into permanent and transitory components reveals a strong link between persistent shocks and recruitment effort. A one standard deviation permanent shock raises advertisement rates by 10-16% of a standard deviation, whereas transitory shocks show no significant effect. These results highlight the importance of shock persistence in labor demand and offer empirical support for dynamic search-and-matching models of the labor market.

title: Irrational Unwillingness in SEP Licensing
affiliations: The University of Science and Technology Beijing

detail.title: Irrational Unwillingness in SEP Licensing
detail.abstract: The role of injunctions in guiding standard-essential patent (SEP) licensing negotiations is important but remains unclear. Many SEP holders argue that a high threshold for injunctions fails to protect them against holdout and efficient infringement. By contrast, SEP implementers are concerned about patent holdup resulting from threats of injunctions by SEP holders. This conflict raises a broader policy issue: how should legal institutions guide parties toward efficient licensing negotiations? However, since the United States withdrew its most recent guidance in 2021, it has lacked a clear position on this issue. Other jurisdictions likewise face challenges in designing effective injunction rules. Among these challenges, the definition of unwilling licensees, a key factor in granting injunctions, remains inconsistent and under development. This Article addresses the unsettled role of injunctions in SEP licensing negotiations and contributes to the policy debate by analyzing cognitive and structural barriers to implementer cooperation. Specifically, it examines whether injunction rules can be designed to effectively enhance the willingness of implementers to license. To that end, it reviews public feedback submitted in a semi-structured survey, which was conducted by the United States Department of Justice in 2022. The survey examined both the thresholds for injunctions and the standards for identifying unwilling licensees. This Article documents various approaches to identifying unwilling licensees, as suggested in the feedback. Based on the documented feedback and textual analysis, the Article identifies four motivations that underline SEP implementers' lack of cooperation in licensing negotiations: 1) resistance to holdup, 2) information asymmetries, 3) habitual holdout and efficient infringement, and 4) financial constraints. These motivations reflect not only strategic behavior but also deeper cognitive biases held by both SEP holders and implementers. This Article argues that due to the cognitive biases, injunction rules, regardless of their design, face inherent limitations in promoting efficient licensing.

title: An Experimental Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis via Coherent Graphene Lattices
affiliations: Independent Research Center "Meta-Algorithmics"

detail.title: An Experimental Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis via Coherent Graphene Lattices
detail.abstract: For over 160 years, the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), which posits that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2, has remained the most celebrated unsolved problem in mathematics. Its proof would have profound implications for number theory and physics. This paper presents an experimental proof of the RH by recontextualizing it not as a purely mathematical conjecture, but as an emergent physical law within the framework of Principia Coherentia (PC). We model a graphene monolayer with a quasicrystalline distribution of icosahedral defects, a system predicted by PC to exhibit SO(5) symmetry. Using experimental data from scanning tunneling spectroscopy (Nature 607, 480-485; Science 367, 648-652), we demonstrate a direct mapping between the energy spectrum of this system's Landau levels and the imaginary parts of the non-trivial zeros of the zeta function. We prove that the system's fundamental drive towards maximal Coherence (max(C)), mathematically expressed through an SO(5)-symmetric unitary transformation (), forces the spectrum-and thus the zeros-onto the critical line Re(s) = 1/2 with an experimental precision exceeding. We conclude that the Riemann Hypothesis is no longer a hypothesis, but an experimentally verified law of nature, a consequence of the quasi-crystalline geometry of space-time predicted by Principia Coherentia.

title: Koopman in LOA: Horizon of Emergence
affiliations: University of Birmingham

detail.title: Koopman in LOA: Horizon of Emergence
detail.abstract: Layered Operator Appraisal (LOA) is a framework for evaluating infrastructure investment by pairing primitives-the direct interventions-with their kernels-the dynamic rules by which effects propagate across the three layers of the human system: society, market, and state. In LOA, appraisal begins from the full operator view and only then, if conditions are met, reduces to Complexity Science (CS) or Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA). Inside the operator, generalised link weights combine structural capacity and reliability, institutional permeability, and information frictions. The Koopman operator offers a rigorous, linear lens on this evolution: it lifts nonlinear state dynamics into a linear evolution of observables, enabling spectral analysis, horizon scaling, and intervention comparison. Yet complex adaptive systems exhibit emergence-a change in the rules themselves-which breaks Koopman's fixed-operator assumption. This paper puts Koopman inside LOA's layered frame, writes the clinical equations, shows how finite projections-Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD)-are estimated, and then explains why emergence breaks semigroup structure and how LOA detects and responds.

title: Expanding the Labor Market Lens: Two New Eurozone Labor Indicators
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and University of Southern California

detail.title: Expanding the Labor Market Lens: Two New Eurozone Labor Indicators

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: International Finance Discussion Papers (Topic)

detail.abstract: We present a principal component analysis of euro area labor market conditions by combining information from 22 labor market indicators into two comprehensive series. These two novel indicators provide a systematic view of the current state and forward-looking direction of the euro-area labor market, respectively, and demonstrate superior forecasting performance compared to existing indicators. Crucially, we find significant implications for monetary policy design: a local projection analysis reveals that ECB monetary policy shocks have attenuated effects on both inflation and unemployment when the labor market forward-looking indicator is high. The dampened inflation response calls for tighter policy rate paths than a standard Taylor rule would prescribe. Finally, we show that focusing solely on the official unemployment rate may understate the actual labor market slack, and consequently, the trade-off between labor market health and inflationary dynamics.

title: Stagflationary Stock Returns
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and International Monetary Fund (IMF) - Research Department

detail.title: Stagflationary Stock Returns

publicationDetails.detailsText: Finance and Economics Discussion Series, issue 2025-056, 2025[10.17016/FEDS.2025.056]

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: We study investors’ perceptions of inflation through the lens of a high-frequency event study, documenting they have a stagflationary view of the world. In response to higher-than-expected inflation, investors expect firms’ nominal cash flows to remain stagnant while discount rates increase, resulting in lower stock prices. Both the equity risk premium and nominal risk-free yields rise, but longer-term real yields remain unchanged. Consistent with investors interpreting inflation as a cost shock, investors expect firms with low market power to suffer larger declines in cash flows. Cash flow expectations of equity investors are aligned with those of professional earnings analysts.

detail.abstract: This research paper explores the transformative impact of disruptive financial technologies on contemporary financial ecosystems, with a particular emphasis on their implications for Syria's financial sector. It presents a comprehensive analysis of blockchain technology, AI-driven analytics, and digital payment systems, critically evaluating their potential to reshape financial structures and operations. The study investigates how these technologies could address the unique challenges and latent opportunities within Syria's financial system-challenges shaped by prolonged conflict, economic sanctions, and restricted access to conventional financial services. It further examines the associated risks and rewards of integrating these innovations in the Syrian context, providing practical insights into necessary regulatory frameworks, infrastructure development, and capacitybuilding measures. The rapid proliferation of disruptive technologies has already driven profound shifts across multiple dimensions of modern economic and social life, and this trajectory is poised to intensify. This research contributes to the scholarly discourse by offering a structured framework for understanding the role of disruptive financial technologies in advancing financial inclusion, fostering economic development, and strengthening resilience in conflict-affected and fragile regions. The ascent of FinTech has accelerated system connectivity and computing capabilities, unlocking vast new streams of actionable data. These advancements hold significant promise for transforming core financial services, including retail banking, investment management, and payment processing, while simultaneously promoting financial literacy and enhancing individual money management practices. The ongoing wave of technological innovation-collectively known as "FinTech"-is driving substantial change within the global financial sector, responding to growing consumer demands for trust, security, privacy, and improved service quality. This new generation of financial technologies spans automated investment advice, peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platforms, mobile payment solutions, blockchain-based transaction systems, and sophisticated algorithms for fraud detection and risk management, all of which are redefining traditional financial models.

detail.abstract: We provide evidence that mega firms have played an increasingly important role in shaping new technological trajectories in recent years. While the share of novel patents---defined as patents introducing new combinations of technological components---produced by mega firms declined until around 2000, it has rebounded sharply since then. Furthermore, we find that the technological impact and knowledge diffusion of novel patents by mega firms have grown relative to those by non-mega firms after 2001. We also explore potential drivers of this trend, presenting evidence that the rise in novel patenting by mega firms is tied to their disproportionate increase in cash holdings and the expansion of their technological scope. Our findings highlight an overlooked positive role of mega firms in the economywide innovation process.

detail.abstract: Prevailing methods for measuring sensitive outcomes confront researchers with an inherent bias-variance trade-off: direct questioning is prone to a sensitivity bias, while indirect methods such as list experiments are substantially less precise. We introduce the ballot-bag, a novel technique that relaxes this trade-off by mitigating bias in direct questioning while improving precision over indirect methods. In a field experiment in Egypt, where direct questions on irregular migration are biased, ballot-bag estimates closely align with those from a list experiment but exhibit significantly lower variance. Consequently, treatment effects are highly significant via the ballot-bag and not via the list experiment.

title: Pricing Lies: Government Contracts and the False Claims Act
affiliations: Pace University - Elisabeth Haub School of Law

detail.title: Pricing Lies: Government Contracts and the False Claims Act
detail.abstract:
Courts have recognized the federal government’s use of government contracts not only as a commercial transaction but also as an instrument of policy. Governments routinely seek to promote small business interests, domestic industry, women-owned, minority-owned, and veteran-owned businesses. However, in cases of fraud involving these policy provisions, courts have consistently failed to recognize this dual nature of government contracts.

The intangible benefits that governments gain from these preferential policies complicate damage calculations for courts when dealing with fraud. Such complications have led to inconsistencies and the emergence of three main approaches. First, some courts have assessed that the government has suffered no damage when it is defrauded with respect to policy compliance and not in relation to the quality of the purchased good or service. The second approach is to award damages for 100% of the contract value. Here, the court reasons that but for the fraudulent misrepresentation, the government would not have awarded the defendant the contract and is therefore entitled to restitution. Finally, some courts calculate damages as the difference between the full value of the contract minus the private market value of the good or service.

In this paper, I argue that the current approaches to calculate fraud damages under the False Claims Act (FCA) are inadequate as they are designed to compensate for damages of a commercial nature and therefore fail to address the damages to the government’s policy interests. This approach ignores the premiums that the government pays to ensure statutory and regulatory compliance by their contractors. To address these issues, instead of looking to the private market value of the good to mitigate the damages caused by the fraud, courts should consider the public market value of the good or service. In other words, instead of applying a reasonable person standard, we should be using a reasonable government standard or a reasonable person, acting on behalf of the government, standard.  The history and purpose of both the FCA and policy objectives in government contracting indicate that Congress intended this type of fraud to be redressed and deterred.

Ultimately, this analysis seeks to provide an understanding of fraud in policy provisions of government contracts and their implications on calculating damages. The article argues for a comprehensive approach that ensures fair compensation for the government while reinforcing broader socioeconomic policy objectives.

title: Hybrid Route-to-Market Algorithms for Direct Selling
affiliations: Universidad del Valle

detail.title: Hybrid Route-to-Market Algorithms for Direct Selling
detail.abstract: Multi-level marketing (MLM) has long struggled with inefficiencies in distribution, inventory planning, and order predictability. In contrast, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies have developed advanced route-to-market (RTM) algorithms that enable high efficiency, scalability, and consistent service levels. This paper proposes the Hybrid FMCG–MLM Methodology, in which FMCG algorithms such as Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), replenishment frequency models, service level optimization, and territory assignment are adapted to MLM contexts. Through case applications in Latin America, the methodology demonstrated significant results: • 35% reduction in stock-outs, • 17-point improvement in on-time delivery, • 18% increase in average order frequency. These findings highlight the potential of adapting FMCG rigor to MLM flexibility, creating a replicable and scalable business methodology. This paper introduces the Hybrid FMCG–MLM Methodology, an original framework that integrates the quantitative rigor of fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) logistics with the entrepreneurial dynamics of multilevel marketing (MLM). Through case studies across industries such as beverages, healthcare, security, and consulting, the research demonstrates measurable improvements in efficiency, scalability, and distributor retention.

detail.abstract: With the accelerated integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into digital healthcare platforms, understanding the operational implications of adopting an AI assistant in telemedicine is crucial. Existing literature highlights AI's potential dual rolescollaborative by recommending appropriate physicians, or competitive by directly offering preliminary medical advice. This study explores how the adoption of AI assistant influence the operational performance of online medical platforms. Leveraging a difference-indifferences (DID) analysis with data from 504 physicians working concurrently on two prominent Chinese online medical platforms-one adopting AI assistance and another serving as a control-we find that the integration of AI significantly increases paid consultations by improving patient-physician matching efficiency. Further heterogeneity analysis reveals stronger AI-driven improvements among physicians affiliated with general departments or elite hospitals, physicians who actively publish articles, and those with high patient satisfaction ratings. These findings advance healthcare operations management literature by demonstrating AI's strategic potential as an effective freemium component, underscoring the importance of considering physician-specific contexts in AI deployment. Practically, our insights offer guidance for healthcare platforms aiming to optimize AI implementation for enhanced operational efficiency and patient engagement.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies can enhance human decision-making in supply chain planning. We experimentally investigate the impact of AI support on human planning decisions in supply chains that require sequential and multi-faceted decision-making. The AI tool, based on deep reinforcement learning, provides human planners with decision suggestions. We design two sets of experiments to examine how planner experience and time pressure influence the effectiveness of the AI tool. In the first experiment set, the AI tool significantly improves the performance of inexperienced planners but has minimal impact on experienced planners. Moreover, it enables inexperienced planners to perform at a level comparable to experienced planners, indicating that AI can, in certain contexts, substitute for human experience. The second experiment set explores the effect of AI support under time pressure. The results show that inexperienced planners learn more slowly and take longer to develop expertise in time-pressured environments. However, AI support substantially enhances their performance even under these challenging conditions. This study contributes to research on AI-human collaboration in decision-making by highlighting the role of AI in boosting the performance of planners with varying experience levels and in highpressure contexts. The findings offer practical implications for the design and deployment of AI systems in supply chain management.

detail.abstract: We study the role of purpose-based rules for behavior and outcomes in a threshold public good game. Rules can be sufficient or even inflated in terms of proposing a fulfilling behavior. We conduct a lab experiment to describe the implications caused by the inflation of a rule. Our study shows that inflated rules are obeyed less. Yet, rule-following occurs also with inflated rules which leads to lower efficiency regarding exactly providing the threshold. A fair share option can help to coordinate efficiently. We complement our analysis by the investigation of the role of the implemented rules for the ex-post optimal behavior, i.e. evaluating the individual contribution depending on the individual payoff.

detail.abstract: We introduce the Credit Adaptation Efficiency (CAE) Index, a novel metric for evaluating how effectively credit markets adapt capital allocation in response to changing risk conditions and borrower quality. The CAE framework is applied to compare private versus public credit markets, using aggregated data from reputable sources (Federal Reserve, BIS, IMF, OECD, S&P LCD, PitchBook, World Bank) to examine three recent stress events: the COVID-19 credit freeze of early 2020, the 2022 interest rate hike cycle, and the 2023 commercial real estate (CRE) stress. We formally define CAE with a mathematical model that relates changes in credit supply to shifts in risk perception, borrower quality, and liquidity conditions. Our results show distinct differences in adaptive behavior: private credit often exhibits a more resilient credit supply during market disruptions, whereas public credit allocation is more sensitive to immediate risk re-pricing. We estimate CAE values for public and private credit in each case study, highlighting instances where private lenders maintained or quickly resumed lending amid rising risk premiums (e.g. during the 2022 tightening, private direct lending AUM grew even as leveraged loan and high-yield bond markets stagnated). The paper discusses implications for institutional investors (e.g. dynamic allocation decisions between public and private debt), for regulators (monitoring systemic resilience via CAE trends), and for market participants (designing strategies to enhance adaptability). We conclude that the CAE Index fills a crucial gap in existing metrics by quantifying structural responsiveness in capital allocation, offering a practical tool to assess market efficiency under stress.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in: Quantum Technology Governance: Law, Policy & Ethics in the Quantum Era, edited by Mateo Aboy, Marcelo Corrales Compagnucci & Timo Minssen (Springer, anticipated late 2025/early 2026)

detail.abstract:
Quantum technologies are emerging as strategic assets with the potential to confer significant economic, technological, and security advantages to governments and corporations that achieve early leadership. As quantum innovations become strategically vital, export controls on these technologies introduce complex legal and policy dilemmas, including tensions between innovation, collaboration, and national security. Quantum computing, in particular, presents unique regulatory challenges due to its layered technological stack and dual-use potential. This chapter offers an in-depth analysis of recent export control measures on quantum computing adopted by the United States and selected European Union Member States. It maps the scope and structure of these controls, examines how they target specific elements of the quantum supply chain, and highlights the shift toward plurilateral regulatory approaches outside traditional multilateral frameworks. Furthermore, it identifies key governance challenges—such as regulating intangible assets, avoiding fragmentation, and adapting to novel quantum paradigms—and provides a forward-looking framework for regulators to design more coordinated and adaptive export control strategies. 

In addition to analyzing constraints, the chapter identifies a range of quantum-specific enforcement opportunities that are uniquely tied to the physical, architectural, and access-layer characteristics of the technology. These include the physical footprint and centralization of large-scale infrastructure, the potential of cloud-based access models for dynamic and differentiated control, and the modular nature of hardware that allows for granular, component-level restrictions. Rather than offering a normative assessment, the chapter distills emerging patterns and strategic considerations likely to shape the future of quantum technology governance. It assesses that there are certain opportunities and challenges of export controls with regard to quantum computers that may inform regulators’ strategy in this space and help guide the design of adaptive, forward-compatible regulatory approaches.

detail.abstract: As part of an institutional initiative to differentiate core undergraduate business classes, we have recently launched a new operations management (OM) course focused on modeling. Whereas the Traditional Operations Management (TOM) course reviews classical models in inventory, queueing, and supply chains, the new Operations Modeling with AI (OMAI) course centers on the practice of mathematical modeling, particularly optimization and simulation. A distinctive element of OMAI is the integration of generative AI-based pair-programming assistants through what we call Incremental Prompting, which prioritizes learning essential modeling skills - abstracting real situations and expressing them with mathematical precision - rather than programming syntax. We evaluated the course through an end-of-term self-assessment survey across both offerings (N = 250; TOM = 156, OMAI = 94). Results indicate that OMAI students reported greater comfort and confidence in understanding, valuing, and applying model-based decision-making. Interestingly, these findings become more pronounced after controlling for prior coding experience, suggesting that OMAI benefits both technically experienced and less experienced learners. In survey responses, students credited the pair-programming framework with their increased comfort and understanding of modeling. Taken together, our findings demonstrate how generative AI can be leveraged in OM and OR education to reduce technical barriers and sharpen focus on core modeling skills.

detail.title: “Green” Technologies as an Indicator of Sustainability, Sustainable Development, and Growth in the Innovation Potential of SMEs

publicationDetails.detailsText: Rozghon, O. V., and Oliukha, V. H. Science and Innovation, volume 21, issue 4, 2025 [10.15407/scine21.04.107]

detail.abstract:
Introduction. In light of the growing risks associated with global warming, the sustainable development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) has gained strategic importance. Their focus on environmental responsibility, the adoption of "green" technologies, and the reduction of ecological impact position SMEs as key contributors to sustainable economic growth. 

Problem Statement. The imperative of environmental protection has necessitated the development and adoption of green technologies. These technologies off er substantial potential for improving the performance and competitiveness of SMEs, particularly within the framework of eco-clusters. 

Purpose. This study aims to examine the legal defi nition and framework of "green" technologies; to assess the feasibility of their implementation by SMEs as members of eco-clusters; to identify the principal areas of legal regulation related to green technologies; and to determine the current level of SME awareness regarding opportunities, benefi ts, and barriers associated with green technology. 

Materials and Methods. The research is based on a combination of general scientifi c and specialized legal methodologies. The source material includes publications by Ukrainian and international scholars, as well as relevant legislation from Ukraine and the European Union.

Results. A comparative analysis of legal doctrine and regulatory practice in Ukraine and the EU has revealed key indicators for guiding the continued green transformation of SMEs in alignment with international standards. Factors influencing SMEs’ awareness of the benefi ts and challenges associated with green technologies have been identified. The study has highlighted the role of eco-clusters as drivers of SME innovation, and has outlined a set of incentive markers essential for motivating SMEs to integrate green technologies in support of sustainable development and responsible environmental behavior. 

Conclusions. The implementation of the green technology concept, as a manifestation of sustainable innovation for SMEs, requires further refinement within Ukrainian legal frameworks. The proposed measures have demonstrated their potential to address pressing environmental issues, mitigate ecological impact, and support climate adaptation strategies. The promotion of green technologies among SMEs, particularly through eco-cluster participation, has emerged as a critical pathway for enhancing their innovation capacity and environmental accountability.

title: Approximation Schemes for Dynamic Pricing with Opaque Products
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School and University of Richmond - Robins School of Business

detail.title: Approximation Schemes for Dynamic Pricing with Opaque Products
detail.abstract:
We study a multi-period, multi-product dynamic pricing problem in which, in addition to traditional (transparent) products, the platform can create and price an opaque product—defined as a virtual product composed of a subset of the displayed transparent products. When a customer selects the opaque option, the platform retains the flexibility to fulfill the order using any of its constituent products. This framework extends classical dynamic pricing models by introducing an additional lever of flexibility through opaque selling, allowing the platform to more effectively balance supply and demand.
We introduce a tractable choice model to capture customer substitution between transparent products and their opaque counterpart. Inspired by the independent demand model, we assume customers arrive with a specific product in mind and substitute only between that product and any opaque option containing it. A key feature of this new choice model is the assumption that customers adopt a pessimistic perspective, valuing an opaque offering based on their least-preferred product included in it. Building upon this model, we devise a constant-factor approximation for the multi-period dynamic pricing problem, leveraging inventory-tracking basis function approximations originally conceived for network revenue management problems. The performance guarantees of our approach depend critically on the ability to solve this single-period version of the problem, which can be viewed as a challenging variant of the classical joint pricing and assortment problem. To address the latter, we develop a quasi-polynomial time approximation scheme (QPTAS), employing novel coupling arguments on customers’ realized opaque utilities to identify collections of opaque options—termed “good” opaque sets—that closely approximate the optimal opaque offering in terms of induced transparent and opaque choice probabilities. Finally, we present extensive numerical experiments demonstrating the practical effectiveness of our algorithmic methods.

detail.abstract:
This paper provides a theoretical examination of the Positive Statistics methodology, a newly developed framework designed to complement and extend conventional statistical practices. Traditional statistics primarily focus on diagnosing problems, failures, and deviations, whereas Positive Statistics reorients statistical analysis toward empowerment, improvement, and the identification of success factors.

The study traces the philosophical and scientific roots of Positive Statistics, drawing on positive psychology, humanistic and existential perspectives, and applied statistics. It introduces the core principles and analytical tools of the methodology, including the Positive Empowerment Index (PEI), the Coverage Index (CI), and the Composite Positive Achievement Index (CPAI).

In addition, several applied cases are presented across education, health, sustainable development, infrastructure, and organizational performance, demonstrating the added value of Positive Statistics in capturing incremental improvements and generating constructive interpretations for policy and decision-making.

By establishing both a conceptual foundation and a methodological framework, this paper positions Positive Statistics as a complementary paradigm in applied statistics, aimed at fostering continuous development and constructive knowledge rather than documenting decline alone.

detail.abstract: We investigate intertemporal scope in acquisitions. The intertemporal scope entails the redeployment of a capability that has been used up and then reactivated. The capability we examine is a commercial bank's ability to restructure troubled debt. We study the capability's redeployment when "capable" acquirers buy target banks with a high percentage of bad loans. We argue that smaller banks are more able to redeploy the capability because their smaller size facilitates retrieving the knowledge underlying it. Also, a capable acquirer's improvement in the target's debt should follow a synergy life cycle as the target's bad loans are restructured. Using a triple-differences (DDD) methodology, we find support for our hypotheses and discuss their relevance to research on intertemporal scope and the synergy life cycle.

title: Representation and Career Trajectories of Female Principal Investigators in Clinical Trials, 2009-2023
affiliations: University of Illinois at Chicago - College of Business Administration

detail.title: Representation and Career Trajectories of Female Principal Investigators in Clinical Trials, 2009-2023
detail.abstract: Background Gender disparities persist in clinical trial leadership, with women underrepresented as principal investigators. While previous studies have documented these disparities, they have largely relied on limited datasets focused on specific therapeutic areas. Previous studies have also neglected potential gender differences in trialist career trajectories. This study examines gender representation in clinical trial leadership using the most comprehensive dataset available, assessing gender-specific trends over time.   Methods We analyzed a large sample of clinical trials submitted to ClinicalTrials.gov from 2010 to 2023. PI gender was inferred using algorithmic classification based on first names. We estimated the probability of female PI leadership for each trial year adjusting for trial characteristics. To assess career trajectories, we examined the number of trials led by male and female PIs within fixed time horizons .   Results Among nearly 160,000 trials analyzed, female representation increased from 32% in 2010 to 41% in 2023. Female PI leadership remained lowest in cardiovascular trials (20%) and highest in behavioral intervention trials (50%). Although male PIs lead more trials than female PIs over all horizons after entering the field, the gap has narrowed over time.     Conclusions Although female PIs remain underrepresented in clinical trial leadership, the gap is narrowing, particularly in terms of early-career progression. Future research should explore the underlying causes of these trends, including bias, career-family trade-offs, and specialty preferences. Additionally, recent evidence suggests female PIs may positively impact trial performance, particularly in patient recruitment diversity and safety outcomes, highlighting the broader significance of gender equity in clinical research.

detail.abstract: Business communication and educational systems in many nations heavily rely on the English language. Thus, the requirement for proficient English communication skills has led to a huge demand for high-quality English language instruction. As one of the least studied topics in the Ethiopian context, the current study was carried out to ascertain how teachers and students felt about teaching listening skills in EFL classes. The study used a descriptive research design to accomplish its goals. Eight (8) lecturers who were teaching English classes were interviewed, and 40 students were given a questionnaire to complete in order to gather data. After being sorted and subjected to both quantitative and qualitative data analysis methods, the data collected by both instruments was thematically interpreted. The study's main conclusions indicate that students frequently miss out on the benefits of classroom English training because they perceive listening skills as a challenging language to master because of their pronunciation. This is due to the lack of facilities and pertinent materials for teaching listening skills, which has left both teachers and students appearing unfamiliar with listening tactics.

title: Perceptual Arbitrage: A Theory-based View of New Ideas and their Effects on Factor Prices
affiliations: University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business

detail.title: Perceptual Arbitrage: A Theory-based View of New Ideas and their Effects on Factor Prices
detail.abstract: The resource-based view of the firm has long held the position that factor markets are efficient, so firms should not be able to acquire resources at rent-generating prices. Recent work in the theory-based view of the firm has challenged this position, arguing that cognition-especially theorization-may enable economic actors to perceive novel uses for factor-market resources (even commodities) that other actors do not, leading actors to detect non-obvious value in resources. Yet this work has been largely theoretical in nature and has not yet drawn a connection between resource search and resource valuation. I extend this work by developing a conceptual model to explain how perceptual mechanisms may drive factor pricing itself. I develop an agentbased simulation model to refine the conceptual framework and explore its implications. Ultimately, I argue that the perception of novel affordances in common resources enables the perceiving agent to acquire resources-even commodity resources-at rent-generating prices, a phenomenon I call perceptual arbitrage. This paper contributes to the resource-based view by presenting a novel theoretical model for what constitutes superior expectations and how such expectations materialize. To the theory-based view of the firm, it contributes a novel quantitative model of the effect of theorization on factor-market arbitrage through factor-market pricing.

title: Constructing a Model of Leadership Behaviours for Achieving Competitive Advantage in RMG Bangladesh: Perspective of a Developing Country

detail.title: Constructing a Model of Leadership Behaviours for Achieving Competitive Advantage in RMG Bangladesh: Perspective of a Developing Country
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study had been toconstruct a model of leadership behaviours for achieving competitive advantage in the ready made garments sector of Bangladesh from the perspective of adeveloping country. The literature review highlighted that leadership behaviours have been studied concerning competitive advantage duly, and they emerged as a separate theme from the literature. However, they have not been conceptualised into a comprehensive framework, which is addressed in this study. Three types of leadership behaviours had been found influencing competitive advantage for an organisation. We hypothesised that task oriented, people oriented, and change oriented leadership behaviours have a significant correlation with a competitive advantage. We surveyed 400 RMG employees, operators, supervisors, executives, and leaders. We found that three types of leadership behaviours alone do not significantly contribute to achieving competitive advantage. However, when emotional intelligence mediates these three behaviours with a competitive advantage, they significantly contribute. Therefore, the present study has developed a conceptual model indicating the relationship between different leadership behaviours, emotional intelligence, and competitive advantage. The model has been developed for Bangladesh's RMG industry due to the paucity of research on leadership behaviours. This article's contribution is part of a dissertation to knowledge is threefold: 1) Practical Implications: Policy implications for the RMG sector, Implementing the recommendations for solving the problem of leadership and gaining competitive advantage. 2) Theoretical Implications: adding change oriented behaviour with task and people oriented ones in the theoretical framework, experimenting with emotional intelligence as a mediating factor. 3) Continuation of research and methodological implications by a time series longitudinal study,cohort studies for other manufacturing groups-contexts. They are initiating a new line of inquiries likedigital leadership in apparel industries.

title: Jesters at Work: Humor Builds Informal Informational Infrastructure
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis, Olin School of Business and Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: Jesters at Work: Humor Builds Informal Informational Infrastructure
detail.abstract: We theorize that humor contributes to an organization's informal informational infrastructure. In this novel perspective, humor facilitates the transmission of work-relevant informationparticularly potentially-threatening content such as dissent and negative feedback-to flow through hierarchical systems. In the process, we draw a distinction between incidental humor that pauses work and integral humor that is about work. We draw from the historical case of the English court jester, whose humor provided monarchs not only with merriment but perspectives, gossip, and difficult truths. Three case studies illustrate how court jesters' humor was relationally embedded within a close dyad and provided the monarch with primary and secondary information to enhance their effectiveness. A typology of four modern jestering types includes the organizational jester, whose work is closest to the medieval role. In what we call the problem of emergence, jesters are least likely to emerge where they are most valuable, namely environments with low psychological safety, negative emotional climate, or high threat rigidity. Implications are discussed for research and practice to conceptualize humor as part of the informal information infrastructure in modern organizations.

title: Protecting the Majority, Restraining the Minority: Constitutionalism in the Wake of the Second World War and Israel’s Early Constitutional Debate
affiliations: Brandeis University

detail.title: Protecting the Majority, Restraining the Minority: Constitutionalism in the Wake of the Second World War and Israel’s Early Constitutional Debate
detail.abstract: This article analyzes how demographic dynamics between Jews and Palestinian-Arabs during Israel's founding years influenced the country's constitutional debate, highlighting a largely unrecognized factor: the central role of the national conflict in shaping Israel's constitutional trajectory. This examination also challenges the prevailing view that post-World War II constitutionalism primarily aimed to protect minorities and limit majority rule, revealing instead how demographic concerns informed constitutional choices. Drawing on archival sources, the study shows that the nascent Jewish majority's primary concern was that the Arab minority might leverage its influence to destabilize the political system. Consequently, the Jewish majority perceived the constitution as a majoritarian tool essential for securing control over state institutions. As a result, fundamental rights and constitutional review-typically core elements of constitutional frameworks-were considered secondary or even unnecessary in this context. Over time, as the Jewish majority stabilized, the urgency for a formal constitution diminished, allowing majoritarian governance principles to take precedence. Israel thus presents a postwar case where constitutionalism was driven by the interests of a numerically insecure majority rather than by minority protections. This analysis underscores how "sufficiently numerous" and "not sufficiently numerous" do not always align with traditional notions of majority and minority.

detail.abstract: This report examines how water is becoming a strategic asset amid rising climate pressures, population growth, and geopolitical tensions. Once a symbol of cooperation, shared water systems are now flashpoints for conflict, with countries like India, Turkey, and China leveraging their upstream control to influence downstream neighbors. Treaties such as the Indus Waters Treaty are being challenged by shifting power dynamics and outdated frameworks. In Pakistan, internal water disputes between provinces, cities and farms, and public versus corporate interests reveal a system strained by mistrust and ecological stress. Climate change is compounding these problems, with melting glaciers, extreme weather, and poor infrastructure leaving millions vulnerable. The report calls for urgent reforms: expanding water storage, adopting climate-smart agriculture, integrating technology, and revising outdated treaties. Without proactive governance and regional cooperation, water will increasingly fuel instability rather than sustain life.

title: Option-Implied Risk Premia with Intertemporal Hedging
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Amherst - Isenberg School of Management, ESSEC Business School and Barclays Bank International

detail.title: Option-Implied Risk Premia with Intertemporal Hedging
detail.abstract: The equity and variance risk premia at a horizon T 1 depend on the risk of changes in the future economic environment beyond T 1. We derive novel estimates of these risk premia that account for intertemporal risk hedging and embed information on the market's term structure of risk. Crucially, our risk premia can be measured ex ante using option prices. We find that intertemporal hedging accounts for up to 80% of the equity and variance risk premia. In particular, intertemporal hedging increases the equity risk premium and decreases the variance risk premium in times of market expansion, characterized by long investors' horizons. Our estimates improve the out-of-sample R2 of market return prediction by a factor of up to 2.

title: Poverty of Kumal Community in Nepal (A Case Study of Ammarpur VDC, Gulmi District, Nepal)
affiliations: Nepal Open University(NOU)

detail.title: Poverty of Kumal Community in Nepal (A Case Study of Ammarpur VDC, Gulmi District, Nepal)
detail.abstract:
Poverty has become a crucial issue, causing significant social and economic disturbances. It generates various social evils such as dissatisfaction, anger, anxiety, and desperation. Poverty is a multidimensional phenomenon that extends beyond lack of income, encompassing health, education, nutrition, employment deprivation, and limited social and political participation. In developing countries like Nepal, poverty is predominantly concentrated in rural areas. Addressing poverty is vital for reducing inequality, eliminating social evils, and promoting social justice.

This study examines the nature and extent of poverty in Amarpur VDC, wards 1–3 of Gulmi district, Nepal, with a focus on the Kumal community. A total of 184 individuals, representing 14.73% of the Kumal population, and 30 households were selected as samples. Findings reveal that 37.62% of the sample population is illiterate, with female literacy lower than male literacy. Most households (63.33%) depend on agriculture and labor, while only 10% engage in business and 3.33% in foreign employment. Land ownership is limited, with 13.33% landless and 56.66% owning less than four ropanis. The Gini coefficient of 0.711 indicates high income inequality, and the mean per capita income stands at Rs.0.83 per day. Educational attainment is low, with only five individuals pursuing bachelor ’ s-level studies.

title: Exploring a New Paradigm for Shock-Resistant Cryptocurrencies: The Crisis-Resilient Composite Token (CRCT)
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Exploring a New Paradigm for Shock-Resistant Cryptocurrencies: The Crisis-Resilient Composite Token (CRCT)
detail.abstract: The digital asset ecosystem continues to expand, yet most cryptocurrencies remain highly volatile and struggle to provide reliable capital preservation during periods of financial stress. This paper introduces the Crisis-Resilient Composite Token (CRCT), a proof-of-concept digital asset designed to balance growth participation with downside protection. The CRCT is constructed from a dynamically rebalanced portfolio that blends decentralized assets (cryptocurrencies, commodities) with traditional financial instruments (equities, bonds, fiat proxies). Using a simple dual-condition framework-based on rolling returns and Sharpe Ratio thresholds-the allocation adapts across regimes, shifting between growth-oriented and defensive positions. Backtesting against major asset classes, stablecoins, and commodities demonstrates that CRCT exhibits lower drawdowns and stronger riskadjusted performance compared to many benchmarks, while maintaining upside participation during favorable markets. This work highlights the potential of hybrid, rule-based allocation in digital finance, bridging decentralized infrastructure with established portfolio principles. While still at a conceptual stage, the CRCT framework illustrates a pathway toward digital instruments engineered for resilience across crises. Future research will extend this design through smart contract automation, transaction cost modeling, and real-world implementation.

title: The Impact of Environmental Protection Tax Policy on Corporate Green and Low-Carbon Technological Innovation: Evidence from China

detail.title: The Impact of Environmental Protection Tax Policy on Corporate Green and Low-Carbon Technological Innovation: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: This study theoretically examines the impact of China’s Environmental Protection Tax Policy (EPTP) on corporate green and low-carbon technological innovation. Using the EPTP as a quasi-natural experiment and employing data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2022, we empirically assess the effect of the EPTP on green and low-carbon technological innovation using a multi-period difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD) approach. Our findings indicate that, compared with firms unaffected by the EPTP, the policy significantly enhances green and low-carbon technological innovation among enterprises in heavily polluting industries in regions with higher environmental tax rates. Mechanism analysis reveals that the policy promotes corporate green and low-carbon technological innovation by alleviating financing constraints and increasing environmental legitimacy pressure. Heterogeneity analysis demonstrates that the policy has a more pronounced effect on large-scale enterprises, firms in regions with higher market competition, and companies in high-tech industries. Further analysis suggests that the EPTP primarily promotes substantive green and low-carbon technological innovation, with no significant impact on strategic green and low-carbon technological innovation. Additionally, the policy significantly and positively affects the green and low-carbon technological innovation of firms at higher quantiles, particularly those with higher green and low-carbon technological innovation levels.
